analysis.requirement: R8 — Broader significance: an ERL-style venue requires a conclusion beyond a single Portland simulation (e.g., across multiple cities/smoke events, nominal capacity produced little benefit while communication/transportation constraints remained unresolved). This demands multi-event or multi-city evidence, or an explicit analytic transportability argument.
exists_defensible: Honest single-city scoping that would survive review as scoping (though not as breadth): research question, intro, and conclusion are explicitly Multnomah/2020 ('This chapter asks what would happen if the same smoke arrived today' — docs/chapter/Capacity_Is_Not_Access.tex:100-101, 110-113; 'If Multnomah County can add clean-air shelter capacity...' — docs/chapter/capacity-is-not-access-source.md:319). The project largely does NOT manufacture breadth it lacks.

One properly hedged hazard-type generalization paragraph, framed as a testable hypothesis rather than a finding: 'The same structure ... applies to extreme-heat cooling centers, warming shelters, and emergency distribution points. The finding that capacity added at existing sites is claimed first by whoever walks fastest is a hypothesis those settings could test' (docs/chapter/Capacity_Is_Not_Access.tex:1081-1086; docs/chapter/capacity-is-not-access-source.md:323).

Mechanism results with structural, plausibly transportable character (candidates for analytic generalization, not yet generalized): the forced arithmetic identity 578 empty = 550 refused + 28 unreachable at capacity==demand (tex:58-62); the dispersion-not-optimizer random-pool control (tex:62-66); the knife-edge scarcity-band finding — 5% surplus matches optimized placement, 10% dissolves the equity gap (tex:70-74, 1060-1067), backed by 21 archived sweep runs (docs/runs/phaseD-bed-sweep/BS080..BS160 x seeds 42-44, verified by directory enumeration).

Multi-severity counterfactual evidence WITHIN the one city: Scenario-E v1 (1.75x) and v2 (Canberra-anchored 4.436x, peak 2,496.1 ug/m3) runs show the structural findings persist at the worst verified urban smoke severity on record — 'awareness still caps arrival (~19% sheltered) ... placement and triage remain inert for WHO gets in' — with every magnitude explicitly labeled counterfactual, never observed (docs/critique-response/13-PHASE-E-PREDICTIONS.md:407-415). Note these results are repo-only; they appear in neither manuscript form.

Multi-draw disruption-configuration robustness protocol: three committed closure draws expose a draw-dependent sign flip in refusal redistribution — 'a single-schedule design would have reported whichever sign its one draw happened to produce' (docs/critique-response/13-PHASE-E-PREDICTIONS.md:376-385) — methodological discipline a reviewer would credit, though still one city.

A literature-anchored multi-event evidence base used for PARAMETERS (not outcomes): the v2 severity anchor is computed from ACT Government raw hourly records for Canberra Florey (2,496.1, with the ~5,000 AQI-vs-concentration correction documented), Fort McMurray 5,229 is cited as the deliberately-unused ceiling with reasons, and closure timing is anchored to five documented events (Camp Fire, Delta, Lahaina, Almeda, Palisades) (docs/final/THE_COMPLETE_STORY.md:1309-1339). This shows the project can do disciplined cross-event work when it chooses to.

Geography/data contains only Portland/Multnomah inputs (RLIS streets, Multnomah AQS PM2.5, Portland IRP campsites, Multnomah shelter CSVs) plus unloaded stock Repast Chicago demo files; the full docs/runs archive (150+ simulation.json manifests enumerated: final-baseline, present-day-three-arm, scenario-d, scenario-crandom, historical-reference, phaseD-bed-sweep, phaseD-windows, phase-e, scenario-e families) is exclusively Portland.

The only measured series is Sept 2020 Multnomah AQS; the 'severe' and 'worst-case' series are deterministic transforms of that same series, and the repo documents why no real foreign series was imported: a county-uniform mean would dilute a spatially localized plume (docs/final/THE_COMPLETE_STORY.md:1327-1330, assumption A-33).

ABSENT: any cross-city or cross-event comparison of nominal shelter capacity vs observed uptake — the exact evidence form the R8 conclusion needs. The repo holds one such data point (Portland 2020: ~130 observed of 198 beds, docs/final/README_RESULTS.md per inventory) and never assembles analogs from Canberra, Seattle, Sacramento, or anywhere else.

The introduction motivates entirely from Portland's own 2020 experience (tex:81-101); a grep for other-city/regional framing (Seattle, West Coast, heat dome, climate, etc.) in the tex returns only the CASPEH California homelessness study and EJScreen/CalEnviroScreen method citations (tex:134, 182, 1233-1235). Related work positions against METHODS (static screening, Siam et al. evacuation ABM, tex:130-156), never against other cities' smoke-shelter experiences.

ABSENT: any formal transportability argument — no statement of which findings are claimed to depend on Portland-specific inputs vs on structure, despite the registry's evidence-class ledger (L/T/A census) containing the raw material for one.

ABSENT (REPORTED from inventory, docs/critique-response/13-PHASE-E-PREDICTIONS.md:253-257): even the registered within-city smokeScale sweep (0.857/1.143) never ran, so no continuous severity dose-response exists — only the three discrete series (1x, 1.75x, 4.436x).

ABSENT: Scenario-E multi-severity results in the manuscript — the closest thing the project has to multi-event evidence lives only in critique-response docs and run archives, contributing nothing to a submission as written.
implementable_with_existing_data: Within-city demand-distribution holdout (the manuscript's own listed extension #4): Geography/data/encampments/irp_campsite_reports_sample.csv carries a per-row inc_date spanning 2025-01-08..2026-07-23 (3,400 rows, verified by the data agent); fit the scenario-C placement on early-window reports and evaluate on late-window reports. Directly answers 'optimizer evaluated on fitted demand' (tex:1077-1079; md:321) and demonstrates robustness across demand realizations — a real, cheap generality increment within one city.

Smoke-severity response surface: the smokeScale and smokeSeriesCode parameters exist in the certified model (Geography/src/geography/agents/ContextCreator.java:510-535 per inventory; websim/docs/PORT_MAP.md:333); run a dense smokeScale grid over the observed 2020 series (including the registered-but-unrun 0.857/1.143 points) to produce access/exposure/equity vs severity curves. Existing data only; converts three discrete severities into a continuous within-city severity claim.

Promote already-archived robustness families into the manuscript: the capacity sweep (docs/runs/phaseD-bed-sweep, 21 runs, verified present), the v1/v2 severity arms and three closure draws (docs/runs/scenario-e*, docs/critique-response/13-PHASE-E-PREDICTIONS.md:376-415) — a 'robustness across event intensities and disruption configurations' section requires zero new runs, only writing, and is the strongest existing partial answer to R8.

Analytic restatement of the knife-edge finding in dimensionless form from archived sweep outputs: express sheltered fraction and equity gap as functions of surplus fraction s = capacity/demand (data already in docs/runs/phaseD-bed-sweep summaries and docs/PRESENTATION_PROVENANCE.md sweep table), and state the scarcity-band condition (gap is a phenomenon of s~1) as the candidate general law other cities would test.

A comparative-severity positioning table from evidence already in-repo: Portland 562.7 (measured), Canberra Florey 2,496.1 (ACT dataset 94a5-zqnn, corrections documented), Fort McMurray 5,229 ceiling with exclusion rationale, plus the five-event closure-timing evidence in A-34 (docs/final/THE_COMPLETE_STORY.md:1309-1339) — supports an honest 'where Portland 2020 sits among documented events' framing paragraph without new acquisition.
needs_new_empirical_data: Second-city awareness/uptake survey (the analog of the Hines N=73 Portland survey that supplies pAwareInit=0.356): retrospective structured survey of unsheltered residents in another smoke-affected city about shelter awareness, attempt, and barriers during a specific event — required before the 'communication constraints remained unresolved across cities' half of the R8 conclusion can be evidenced; no such dataset exists in any city per the project's own literature search (docs/science/phase2-human-agents/04-DECISION.md per inventory).

Prospective occupancy/turnaway logging agreement for the NEXT Portland smoke event (instrument: per-facility hourly headcount + turnaway tally kept by shelter operators, negotiated with JOHS) — the only way to move beyond the single newsroom snapshot if archival records genuinely do not exist, and a prerequisite for calibrated multi-event claims even within one city.
needs_external_acquisition: Hourly PM2.5 for candidate second cities/events — candidate source: EPA AQS API; the repo already contains the exact fetch pattern (scripts/fetch-aqs-pm25.ps1, verified present), so e.g. Seattle/King County Sept 2020 or Sacramento Nov 2018 series are plausibly one script-parameter change away (availability of adequate in-county monitor coverage unchecked).

Second-city street network — candidate sources: OpenStreetMap extracts or municipal GIS (e.g., Seattle SDOT, DataSF); would require a new ingestion path since the model currently reads RLIS shapefiles.

Second-city shelter inventory and unsheltered population — candidate sources: HUD CoC/PIT published counts and county human-services shelter lists (the Portland workflow used exactly this class of source); comparability of capacity units would need the same conversion audit done here.

Second-city encampment-location proxy — candidate sources: municipal 311/complaint open-data feeds (e.g., Seattle Find It Fix It, SF 311). NOTE: the Portland IRP feed's known biases (complaint-driven, rolling window) would recur, and no availability check has been performed.

Observed occupancy/turnaway records for other cities' smoke-shelter activations — candidate holders: King County (2020), Sacramento/Butte County (2018 Camp Fire smoke), ACT Government (Canberra 2019-20) after-action reports, likely via records requests; this is the direct evidence for a cross-event 'nominal capacity vs realized uptake' table. The Portland experience warns these may not exist (the county's own record reduced to one newspaper article, docs/final/SHELTER_CAPACITY_AUDIT.md:158-166 per inventory).

The real measured Canberra hourly series (ACT open data 94a5-zqnn) — already located and verified by the project but deliberately not imported because the county-uniform field would dilute a localized plume (docs/final/THE_COMPLETE_STORY.md:1327-1330); acquiring it plus a defensible spatial treatment would upgrade the worst-case arm from counterfactual transform to real second event.

claims_exceeding_evidence.claim: "The policy sentence that survives every control is: buy surplus if you can; where you cannot, the triage reserve buys the same equity for free."
claims_exceeding_evidence.why: An unconditioned, imperative policy generalization ('survives every control') derived from one county, one smoke series, one model whose access figures are self-declared upper bounds (tex:75-76). All the controls it survives are internal to the same Portland system; nothing establishes the advice transfers to any other city, which is precisely what R8 would require before stating it as a portable policy rule.

claims_exceeding_evidence.claim: "The approach generalizes beyond smoke." (opening sentence, present-tense declarative)
claims_exceeding_evidence.why: The paragraph's closing sentence correctly downgrades to 'a hypothesis those settings could test', but the topic sentence asserts generalization as accomplished. No cooling-center, warming-shelter, or distribution-point application has been attempted anywhere in the repo; 'may generalize' is what the evidence supports.

claims_exceeding_evidence.claim: "The present 36-facility system shelters 30.1% of residents." and "the same 6,842 spaces more than halve refusals depending only on placement"
claims_exceeding_evidence.why: Present-tense claims about the real system, uncondition-ed in-sentence (hedged only elsewhere, md:289). Under R8 this matters doubly: a reader extracting a broader lesson will treat single-city model output as an empirical finding about shelter systems generally, when it is an upper-bound simulation under universal awareness in one county.

claims_exceeding_evidence.claim: Symposium deck attribution headline: optimizer contributes zero to headcount and 63.1% shorter walks (REPORTED — verified by the manuscript agent at docs/final/presentation/capacity-is-not-access-symposium.html:335, not re-read by me)
claims_exceeding_evidence.why: If the deck circulates alongside any broader-significance repositioning, its headline-style single-city control-comparison numbers carry none of the chapter's scoping and would read as general findings about siting optimization.

proposed_methods: Two-city (minimum) comparative replication with harmonized public inputs: OSM/municipal street network, EPA AQS smoke series for that city's event, HUD PIT + county shelter inventory, 311-feed encampment proxy; run the identical A/B/C/capacity-sweep protocol with pre-registered per-city predictions (reusing the project's proven Phase-D/E registration discipline, docs/critique-response/12- and 13-PREDICTIONS.md); report outcomes in dimensionless form (access vs surplus fraction s, equity gap G(s), knife-edge location) so cities are comparable.

Cross-event observed-uptake meta-table (no simulation required): nominal activated capacity vs documented occupancy for every locatable smoke-shelter activation (Portland 2020 ~130/198 plus acquired records for e.g. King County 2020, Sacramento 2018, Canberra 2019-20) — the most direct possible support for 'nominal capacity produced little benefit while communication constraints remained unresolved', and it converts the project's n=1 calibration weakness into a comparative finding.

Analytic/dimensional generalization of the knife-edge and dispersion results: a coverage/queueing or p-median-theoretic argument expressing sheltered fraction as a function of surplus fraction and a network-reach parameter, validated against the archived BS080-BS160 sweep — states the CONDITIONS under which surplus dominates siting, which is a transferable claim a single city can legitimately originate.

Formal transportability audit built from the existing registry: use the L(ocal)/T(ransferred)/A(ssumed) evidence-class census in Geography/data/registry/variables.csv to state explicitly which mechanisms depend on Portland-specific inputs vs on structure (selection-diagram-style reasoning), turning the honest parameter ledger into the manuscript's generalization argument.

Within-city robustness package implementable now: temporal fit/evaluate split of the campsite feed by inc_date; smokeScale response-surface grid; promotion of the archived v1/v2 severity and closure-draw ranges into a manuscript robustness section — collectively a defensible 'robust across demand realizations, severities, and disruption configurations within one city' claim.

Venue-honest alternative: keep the current Springer-chapter scope (single-city mechanistic case study — its actual posture, SUBMIT.md:81,178) or, for ERL, reframe the contribution as mechanism-plus-method with the multi-city protocol as the stated research program, and add the comparative-events positioning table — rather than asserting breadth the evidence base cannot carry.
analysis.priority_rationale: For the deliverable as it actually exists — a Springer edited-volume chapter (SUBMIT.md:81,178) — R8 is low-stakes: the chapter is candidly Multnomah-scoped, its one generalization paragraph is hedged as a hypothesis, and no chapter reviewer is likely to demand multi-city evidence. For an ERL repositioning, R8 is dispositive and currently unmet at the desk-rejection level: every outcome number in 150+ archived run manifests derives from one county under one observed smoke series (or deterministic transforms of it), external calibration is a single newsroom observation, and the manuscript contains zero multi-city motivation, positioning, or evidence. The requirement also interlocks with the project's other weakest points: the exact broader conclusion ERL would want ('nominal capacity produced little benefit while communication constraints remained unresolved') rests, on the communication side, on one N=73 retrospective survey and one newspaper sentence about 211 waits — local evidence that cannot support a cross-city clause. What depends on R8: the transferable value of the project's genuinely strong results (the capacity-access identity, the dispersion-vs-optimization control, the knife-edge scarcity band, the free triage-reserve equity fix) — these are structurally the kind of findings that generalize, but nothing yet demonstrates it. The cheapest genuine progress, in order: (1) the cross-event observed-uptake table (external acquisition only, directly evidences the R8 sentence); (2) the analytic dimensionless restatement plus transportability audit (existing data); (3) one second-city replication via the harmonized-public-data pipeline. Absent at least (1) or (3), the defensible move is to keep the single-city chapter framing and not submit breadth claims to ERL.
